spring_break_note: University of Miami spring break 2027 is 6-13 March, which sits directly on top of the second date window. Practical consequences: (1) Miami Beach and Wynwood lodging that week runs 15-25% above the rest of early March and the good boutique stock is commonly sold out by December; (2) Nassau and Paradise Island are the single worst-value place in the Caribbean that specific week, because US college spring break is exactly what that market prices for — that alone disqualifies the Bahamas even before the budget does; (3) the Florida Keys are unevenly affected — Key West's Duval Street fills with breakers from the first week of March, but Islamorada is a fishing and family island and barely registers it. RECOMMENDED SHAPE: put the Miami leg BEFORE the wave (arrive 2 March, Miami 2-5 March) and the Keys leg 5-9 March. That keeps Miami out of the worst pricing and puts the spring-break week in the one place that does not care. If the flights force you into 6-13 March, book everything by early December and add 20% to every Miami figure below.
beach_verdict: THE FLORIDA KEYS — Islamorada, bayside, in a house. Blunt version: at USD 100 per person per night for five people in early March, the Bahamas and Aruba are not available at any level of compromise. Verified peak-season numbers: Exuma hotels average roughly USD 1,040/night in March, the single most expensive month there, with no budget tier at all and restaurant mains starting at USD 18 — five people need two rooms, so that is USD 400+ pp/night before you eat. Aruba's Palm Beach averages USD 559/night in March; Eagle Beach starts around USD 230 and runs 10-20% above Palm Beach. Turks & Caicos Grace Bay has a USD 229 floor with most decent properties at USD 500-850 and Grace Bay Club at USD 896. Nassau/Paradise Island is nominally the cheapest (deals from ~USD 225, cheapest room seen USD 124, Baha Mar quoting USD 465 for late March) but it is also the one destination that prices specifically against US college spring break, which is exactly the 6-13 March window — it is the worst possible week to be there and the good beach is behind a resort gate anyway. Every one of those three also costs a return flight from MIA (Nassau ~USD 263-279, Exuma ~USD 293, Providenciales ~USD 355 on AA) plus two half-days of travel out of nine, and none of them let you use a rental car you are already paying for. The Keys cost zero extra flights, a 1h45 drive, and they are the only option where five people can share one roof. Be clear-eyed about the number: even in the Keys the honest all-in floor for five is about USD 105-125 pp/night once the cleaning fee, the VRBO/Airbnb service fee and the 12.5-14.5% Monroe County lodging tax are amortised over four nights — a 3-bedroom bayside canal house with a dock at a USD 380-450 headline rate lands at roughly USD 540-590/night all-in, i.e. USD 108-118 pp. Getting genuinely under USD 100 pp means Key Largo rather than Islamorada, bayside rather than oceanfront, and no private pool. HONEST DOWNSIDE: Keys beaches are NOT Caribbean beaches. The natural shoreline is coral rock and mangrove, most 'beach' is trucked-in sand, and inshore water is shallow and grassy. Bahia Honda is the one real exception and it is an hour south. The Keys payoff is ON the water — sandbars, the only living barrier reef in the continental US, boat days — not lying on it. Second caveat: March is the windy season here; cold fronts every 5-10 days bring 15-25kt northerlies that cancel boat trips, so book the charter for the calmest forecast day with a spare day behind it. If pure beach beauty is the actual priority, Great Exuma or Turks & Caicos win outright and the honest advice is to raise the budget to about USD 200 pp/night and accept it. At a hard USD 100 for five people in spring-break week, the Keys are the only truthful answer.

stops.name: Miami
stops.area_note: For a design-conscious group of five, the answer is NOT Ocean Drive. South Beach below 15th Street is the spring-break epicentre in early March and the Art Deco hotels there are loud, overpriced and tired. Two good bases instead: (1) WYNWOOD / EDGEWATER — the actual design and food centre of gravity (Wynwood Walls, Rubell Museum, Margulies, Design District 10 min north, PAMM 10 min south, Boia De and Mandolin nearby). (2) UPPER SOUTH BEACH / COLLINS PARK (17th-30th St) and MID-BEACH (30th-60th) — you still walk to sand but you are north of the mess; Freehand, Esme, Circa 39 and Hotel Rendale all sit here. Brickell is glassy and corporate. Little Havana is great to eat in, fine to sleep in on a budget, but not walkable at night. Coconut Grove is leafy and lovely but sleepy and far from everything on your list. THE NON-OBVIOUS FINDING FOR A 3-NIGHT STAY: in Miami the hotel actually competes with the rental, because a 3-night Airbnb has to amortise a USD 200-300 cleaning fee over only three nights. A good 3BR Wynwood apartment at a USD 550 headline lands near USD 766/night all-in (USD 153 pp), while Freehand with one private quad plus one private double lands near USD 610/night all-in (USD 122 pp) — better located, better designed, no cleaning fee. Flip the logic in the Keys, where four nights amortise the cleaning fee properly and the house wins decisively. RESORT FEE TRAP, and it is worse for five people because the fee is PER ROOM: The Standard Spa charges USD 55 + tax per room per night (some channels list USD 62.70); The Goodtime charges USD 45.60 per room per night plus USD 50 nightly valet; Esme guests report an amenities fee adding ~33% to a three-night bill. Three rooms means you pay that fee three times. Miami Beach lodging tax is about 13% on top. PARKING is per vehicle, not per room — with one rental SUV you pay it once, USD 40-55/night valet on Miami Beach, USD 25-35 at a municipal garage or a mainland lot, and USD 0 if you rent a house with a driveway. BLUNT CONCLUSION FOR MIAMI: five people at USD 100 pp/night in early March does not buy anything beautiful. The only configurations that actually clear USD 100 pp are hostel-style shared rooms at Hotel Rendale (~USD 88 pp) or Freehand (~USD 94 pp in an 8-bed shared). Given the stated preference — rather pay 90 for something beautiful than 50 for something generic — the honest recommendation is to accept roughly USD 120-125 pp in Miami for Freehand privates or a Little Havana house, and claw the difference back in the Keys. activities.name: Wynwood Walls plus the free gallery walk
activities.what: Ticketed Wynwood Walls courtyard, then walk NW 2nd Ave and NW 23rd-26th St for free street art and commercial galleries. Finish at the Rubell Museum in Allapattah (USD 15 adult) — one of the best private contemporary collections in the US. CLOSED Mon and Tue; open Wed/Thu/Sun 11:30-17:30 and Fri/Sat 11:30-19:30.

activities.name: Dinner at Los Felix, Coconut Grove
activities.what: Mexico-City-inspired, house nixtamal, mezcal list. Holds both a Michelin star and a Michelin Green Star in the 2026 Florida guide. Book weeks ahead — a table for five in spring-break week needs to be locked in by January.

activities.name: Design District architecture walk plus PAMM
activities.what: Morning in the Miami Design District: Buckminster Fuller's Fly's Eye Dome, Sou Fujimoto's Palm Court, the Museum Garage facade. Then 10 min south to Perez Art Museum Miami — the Herzog and de Meuron building with its hanging gardens is the real attraction. USD 18 adult. CLOSED Tue and Wed; open late Thu to 21:00.

activities.name: Little Havana Calle Ocho food walk
activities.what: Six tasting stops over 2.5 hours — Cuban sandwich, empanadas, pastelitos, tostones, croquetas, cafe cubano — plus a working cigar roller, Maximo Gomez Domino Park and the Calle Ocho Walk of Fame. USD 69.99-79 pp. Departs 1543 SW 8th St; book 24-48h ahead. Stay on for live son at Ball and Chain.

activities.name: Private boat day on Biscayne Bay (real split for five)
activities.what: Private captained charter from Miami Beach or Downtown: Key Biscayne sandbar, Star Island, the Miami River. GetYourGuide lists a 4-hour private charter at USD 400 for up to 6; open-market motorboats and pontoons run USD 100-300/hour. Budget USD 500 for four hours = USD 100 pp for five, plus ~20% captain tip (USD 20 pp) and bring your own cooler — drinks bought aboard are where the budget dies.
activities.when: Day 3 late morning, pick the calmest forecast day

activities.name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
activities.what: 1916 Italianate villa on Biscayne Bay with formal gardens and the stone barge — the most photogenic place in Miami. Adult admission currently USD 20, reduced from USD 25 during restoration. Go at opening or late afternoon for the light.

activities.name: Key Biscayne bikes, or the Everglades airboat alternative
activities.what: Option A: rent bikes, ride the Rickenbacker Causeway to Crandon Park and the Bill Baggs Cape Florida lighthouse — best beach in Miami-Dade and the best skyline view. Option B if you skip the boat: Everglades Safari Park from USD 30, or Everglades Holiday Park at USD 41.99 + tax including the gator show. Both ~45 min west; go at 09:00 before the coaches.

food.name: Los Felix
food.what: Coconut Grove. Heirloom-corn Mexican, house nixtamal. Michelin star plus Green Star 2026.

food.name: Joe's Stone Crab
food.what: South Beach, since 1913. Stone crab season is October-May so March works. No reservations — arrive at 17:00, or use Joe's Take Away next door for half the price.

stops.weather_note: Early March is the best weather Miami gets. Average highs rise from 78F to 81F (26-27C) across the month, average low 70F (21C), sea temperature about 76F (24C) — swimmable but not warm. March is statistically the DRIEST month: about 6 rainy days, ~53mm total, and the sky is clear or partly cloudy 68% of daylight hours. The real March variable is wind, not rain: cold fronts push down the peninsula bringing two or three days of 15-25kt northerlies that chop up the bay and can cancel boat days. Pack one warm layer for evenings on the water.

stops.name: Islamorada, Florida Keys
stops.area_note: Base: ISLAMORADA, mile markers 74-90 on US-1, about 1h45 from Miami with no traffic (allow 2h30 leaving on a Friday). It is the sweet spot: close enough to lose no travel day, it has the marina and charter infrastructure for the boat day, it has the only real cluster of design-minded places in the Keys (Casa Morada, Amara Cay, Morada Bay), and it does NOT get the Duval Street spring-break scene — which matters a lot given the 6-13 March overlap. Key West is 80 miles further, 2h each way, and in spring-break week it is both the most expensive and the most crowded part of the Keys: treat it as one long day trip, or split 2 nights Islamorada + 2 nights Key West only if Mallory Square and Dry Tortugas outrank the boat day. KEY WEST RENTAL WARNING: the City of Key West bans rentals under 30 days without a transient licence, licences are capped and tied to specific transient-zoned properties, most residential zones prohibit short-term rentals outright, and enforcement is aggressive. A cheap-looking Key West listing is often illegal and can be cancelled on you. Islamorada and Key Largo have no such ban. HOTEL REALITY FOR FIVE PEOPLE — be blunt: there is NO in-budget hotel configuration in Islamorada in early March. Islamorada hotel rates average roughly USD 557/night in March against USD 234 in September, peak December-April rates run 40-60% above shoulder, and waterfront occupancy is above 85% from January to March. Five people need two double-queen rooms or a villa, and the cheapest honest hotel config below still lands at USD 137 pp. THE HOUSE IS THE RECOMMENDATION, NOT A FALLBACK — and unlike Miami, four nights amortise the cleaning fee properly, so it genuinely works. activities.name: Drive Miami to Islamorada, then tarpon at Robbie's
activities.what: 1h45 to 2h30 on US-1. Stop at Alabama Jack's on the Card Sound approach or Key Largo Fisheries. Check in, then Robbie's of Islamorada at MM 77.5 to hand-feed 2m tarpon off the dock — dock access USD 2.50 pp, bait bucket USD 5. Five minutes long, everyone's favourite photo. Stay for sunset at Morada Bay or Lorelei.
activities.duration: Half day driving, 1 hour at Robbie's
activities.when: Day 4, leave Miami by 10:00 to beat the causeway

activities.name: Private sandbar and reef boat day (book this first)
activities.what: Captained charter out of Islamorada for 4-6 hours: the Islamorada sandbar at low tide (waist-deep flats, anchor up, cooler, music), then snorkel Alligator Reef Lighthouse or Cheeca Rocks. Expect USD 600-900 for a private half-day boat for six in peak season, i.e. USD 120-180 pp — the one splurge worth breaking the rule for. Cheaper alternatives at Robbie's: twice-daily group snorkel at 10:00 and 13:30, or party-boat fishing at USD 100 pp morning, USD 75 pp afternoon.
activities.when: Day 5 — but move it to whichever of the four days has the lightest wind

activities.name: Key West day trip: Bahia Honda, Mallory Square sunset
activities.what: 2h each way down the Seven Mile Bridge. Stop at Bahia Honda State Park, MM 37, USD 8 per vehicle — the only genuinely beautiful natural beach in the Keys and worth the stop on its own. In Key West: Hemingway House, Cuban coffee at Cuban Coffee Queen, the Southernmost Point queue, then the free Mallory Square sunset celebration with buskers, starting ~90 min before sunset (about 18:30 in early March). Duval will be full of spring breakers — drink at the Green Parrot instead. Long day, nominate a driver.

activities.name: Snorkel John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
activities.what: 40 min north to Key Largo, MM 102.5. The park's own 2.5-hour guided snorkel boat is USD 45 pp; private operators from USD 50 pp, in-water guide about USD 120 plus USD 70 per extra snorkeller. Shallow patch reefs, the Christ of the Abyss statue, good visibility when the wind is down. Pair it with the History of Diving Museum at MM 83 on the way back — small, odd, genuinely good.
activities.when: Day 7 morning, before the afternoon wind builds

activities.name: Kayak Indian Key, then the last sunset at Morada Bay
activities.what: Free kayaks and SUPs come with most Islamorada resorts and many rental houses. Paddle from Indian Key Fill at MM 79 to Indian Key Historic State Park — the ruins of an 1830s wrecking town on a tiny island. Calm bayside water, no boat needed, and it works even on a windy day. Finish with dinner and sunset at Morada Bay, feet in the sand.

activities.name: Only if you split to Key West: the Dry Tortugas ferry
activities.what: Worth it only with a Key West overnight, because the Yankee Freedom III departs 07:30 and returns 17:30. USD 250 per adult including national park entry, snorkel gear, breakfast and lunch (USD 240 for students). Fort Jefferson, 110km out in the Gulf, is the single best thing in the Florida Keys and comfortably the most expensive. Sells out weeks ahead in March — in spring-break week, book by January.
activities.when: Only with a Key West overnight

food.name: Morada Bay Beach Cafe
food.what: MM 81 bayside. Tables in the sand, the best sunset in the Keys, decent seafood. Pierre's upstairs is the fancy sister. Book a table for five ahead in March.

food.name: Hungry Tarpon at Robbie's
food.what: MM 77.5. Breakfast and fish tacos on the dock, tiny and packed. Eat first, then feed the tarpon.

food.name: Lazy Days Restaurant
food.what: MM 79.9 oceanside. Bring your own catch or order theirs; yellowtail snapper is the order. Straightforward, good, local.

food.name: Chef Michael's
food.what: MM 81.6. The best actual cooking in Islamorada — hogfish and local fish done four ways. Small room, reserve ahead.

food.name: Key Largo Fisheries
food.what: A working fish house with a back-deck counter at MM 99. Cheapest good seafood in the Upper Keys and the right stop on the drive down or back.

stops.weather_note: The Keys run 1-2C warmer than Miami in early March: highs around 27-28C, lows 21-22C, water about 24C, and it is the dry season so rain is minimal. What actually matters is WIND. Late-winter cold fronts sweep through every 5-10 days bringing 15-25kt northerlies for two or three days, which chops up the ocean side, kills reef visibility and gets snorkel and charter trips cancelled. Practical rule: book the boat day for the calmest forecast day of your four, keep a spare day behind it, and hold the bayside kayak plan as the wind-proof backup. Bring long sleeves — an evening on a boat in a March front is genuinely cold.

getting_around: MIAMI NEEDS A CAR and with five people it needs a full-size SUV. Wynwood to the Design District to PAMM to Vizcaya to Little Havana to Key Biscayne is a 40km loop with effectively no public transport between the nodes (the free Metromover only covers Downtown and Brickell). Uber/Lyft works but at five people every single trip is an XL: MIA to South Beach runs roughly USD 35-50, and a day of neighbourhood-hopping easily hits USD 80-120 for the group — two days of that pays for a rental day. A rental SUV from MIA in early March is roughly USD 70-100/day plus about USD 20/day in taxes and fees. THE HIDDEN COST IS PARKING, NOT THE CAR, and it is charged PER VEHICLE not per room, so one car for five is the right answer: Miami Beach hotel valet is USD 40-55/night (The Goodtime charges USD 50), municipal garages USD 2-4/hour, South Beach street parking needs the PayByPhone app, and a rental house with a driveway erases the line item entirely. Argentine licences are accepted in Florida for short visits, but rental companies may ask for an International Driving Permit alongside, every driver must be named on the contract, and under-25 drivers pay a young-driver surcharge — with a late-20s/30s group check whether anyone is still 24. KEYS: the car is mandatory, US-1 is the only road, there is no alternative route, and southbound Friday afternoons and northbound Sunday afternoons are genuinely bad — add an hour. Mile markers descend from 106 in Key Largo to 0 in Key West and everything is addressed by MM. Drink-driving enforcement on US-1 is heavy: nominate a driver for the Key West day, and note that with a house on a canal you can walk to nothing, so someone is always driving. KEEP THE SAME RENTAL for all nine days rather than returning and re-renting — short re-rentals in March price badly.
budget_reality_note: BLUNT VERSION FOR FIVE PEOPLE: USD 100 pp/night in early March in South Florida does not buy anything beautiful, and in the Caribbean it does not buy anything at all. The reason is that five is an awkward number — it means three hotel rooms, or two double-queen rooms, and every per-room fee multiplies. MIAMI, 3 nights: an advertised USD 200 double becomes USD 200 + a per-room resort fee (verified: USD 55+tax at The Standard, USD 45.60 at The Goodtime, an amenities fee at Esme that guests report adding ~33% to a three-night bill) + ~13% lodging tax, and you pay that two or three times over. Three rooms at USD 240 is USD 720/night = USD 144 pp before parking. The rental side is no better at three nights because a USD 250-300 cleaning fee has to amortise over just three: a USD 550 Wynwood 3BR lands at USD 766/night all-in = USD 153 pp. THE ONLY CONFIGURATIONS THAT CLEAR USD 100 pp IN MIAMI ARE HOSTEL-STYLE: five beds in a shared ensuite at Hotel Rendale (~USD 88 pp) or an 8-bed shared at Freehand (~USD 94 pp). Given the stated priority — beautiful at 90 over generic at 50 — the honest recommendation is to accept about USD 122 pp for Freehand's private quad plus a private double, which is the best design-per-dollar configuration in the city for exactly five people, or USD 124 pp for a Little Havana 3BR house with a pool and free parking. KEYS, 4 nights: no hotel works. Islamorada averages roughly USD 557/night in March; the cheapest one-roof hotel answer for five is a 2-bedroom villa at La Siesta at USD 137 pp, and everything else runs USD 170-196 pp. Four nights DO amortise a cleaning fee properly, so the house wins decisively: a Key Largo 3BR canal house at a USD 400 headline lands at USD 556/night all-in = USD 111 pp, and a bayside Islamorada 3BR with a dock at USD 450 headline lands at USD 618 = USD 124 pp. Remember Monroe County lodging tax is 14.5%, higher than Miami-Dade's ~13%. THE HONEST BOTTOM LINE: budget USD 120-125 pp/night for accommodation across both legs rather than USD 100, which is about USD 875 per person for seven nights instead of USD 700 — a USD 175 per person gap. Three ways to close it if the number is hard: drop Miami to 2 nights and add one to the Keys (the cleaning fee amortises better and Miami is the expensive leg); take the Freehand shared-dorm config for the Miami leg only; or move the whole trip to 1-8 March, entirely ahead of the 6-13 March University of Miami spring break, which is worth 15-25% on Miami lodging by itself. SPEND THE SAVED MONEY ON: one private boat day in the Keys (USD 120-180 pp) and one or two serious Miami dinners (USD 95-140 pp at Los Felix or Boia De). TWO LEGAL TRAPS: Miami Beach bans short-term rentals under 180 days in ALL single-family residential zones with fines starting at USD 20,000 and doubling per offence — only the Entertainment District, North Beach Town Center and RM-2/RM-3 are legal, so a cheap Miami Beach house is probably an illegal listing. And the City of Key West prohibits rentals under 30 days without a capped transient licence and enforces hard — do not book a Key West house at all.
